title_en: Traffic accident under the influence of drugs
evidence_excerpt:
Bremen police officers apprehended a 37-year-old man in Arsten on Saturday afternoon. He is suspected of having caused a traffic accident under the influence of drugs, in which a 66-year-old was injured.
At approximately 3:30 PM, a patrol car crew initially came across a Skoda that had crashed into the guardrail on the Arsten motorway feeder road. A group of witnesses was standing by the car, as the driver had apparently suffered a seizure. As the patrol car approached, however, he suddenly accelerated and fled. Approximately one kilometer further on, shortly before the feeder road's exit onto the motorway, he caused another traffic accident. In doing so, he collided with the 66-year-old's Hyundai, which skidded. Emergency services took the driver with head injuries to the hospital. On Arster Heerstraße, the Skoda came to a stop due to the severe damage, and the officers apprehended the 37-year-old. In the car, they found a small amount of cocaine and a box containing presumably illegal performance-enhancing substances. The man stated that he had consumed cocaine overnight. The police officers took him to the station, where a blood sample was ordered. They also filed criminal charges, including for endangering road traffic, negligent bodily harm, and violations of the Narcotics Act. Further investigations by the traffic police department are ongoing.
